clusters.title: I replaced YouTube's app with OpenTubeX and its self-hosted backend, and I don't want to go back
My server, NAS, PC, and Mac all share one Google Drive folder, and none of them run Google's app

xda.author: João Carrasqueira
xda.body:
I replaced YouTube's app with OpenTubeX and its self-hosted backend, and I don't want to go back
As Google's desire to maximize revenue from YouTube grows, the user experience arguably gets worse. Ads are more intrusive than ever, and the service pushes its most popular channels, which are often riddled with low-effort content and so-called "AI slop". So what if you could make YouTube into a more peaceful experience without sacrificing some of the things you love about it?

xda.author: Shekhar Vaidya
xda.body:
My server, NAS, PC, and Mac all share one Google Drive folder, and none of them run Google's app
I have been a Google Drive (now Google One) user for more than a decade. Even after building my own homelab with servers and NAS, I still have cloud storage with me. For my Windows PC and MacBook, it was easy to use Google’s Drive app, but on the Debian server and NAS, there’s no official way.
